messages:
morgan: heads-up: CI microbench on PR #2281 tripped the KV-cache threshold. saw ~8% drop in kv_hit microbench vs baseline, failing the perf gate. link: https://ci.internal/redwood/pr/2281/perf
raj: ack, saw the alert. which test exactly? kv_cache_hit_rate or kv_lookup_latency?
morgan: kv_cache_hit_rate primarily, also small tail latency wobble in batcher microbench. failure diff attached in CI artifact.
perf-bot: [perf/regression] PR 2281: kv_cache_hit_rate -8.2% (threshold -5.0%). job: microbench/kv-cache-v2.
li: oof. PR touches kernel-autoselect and batch-sampler heuristics, right?
morgan: yes — the change in kernel-autoselect introduced a new tiebreaker that biases affinity for concat kernels. hypothesis: this increases split batches and reduces effective kv prefix reuse.
olivia: can we reproduce locally with the failing microbench? share minimal repro command.
raj: trying reproduce now on my dev box (A100 local). running: 
```
# reproduce
git checkout pr/2281
bazel test //bench/micro:kv_cache_bench --test_arg=--runs=200 --profile
```
li: i ran a quick smoke and saw kv hit down ~7% on seqlen=64 distributions. flamegraph shows hot in KernelSelector::choose_kernel() at ~22% (was 6% before).
kai: interesting — that aligns with the theory that the tiebreaker is doing extra work or iterating more candidates. can you paste the flamegraph snippet?
li: pasted small snippet: 
```
22% KernelSelector::choose_kernel()
  12% CandidateScanner::evaluate_costs()
   6% AffinityComparator::compare()
    3% quantize_cost_estimate()
```
morgan: thanks. Raj — can you run a git bisect to see which commit introduced the perf delta?
raj: starting bisect now. steps: 
```
git bisect start 8423457000 abc123def
git bisect run ./tools/bench/ci_bench_runner.sh --target microbench/kv-cache-v2
```
raj: quick update: bisect points to commit `c4f7a9d` (kernel-autoselect: add affinity tiebreaker + heuristics).
morgan: nice narrowing. is there a smaller repro that isolates just the selector cost (no KV backend)?
li: yes, bench includes a selector-only mode: `--selector-only`. running that shows selector CPU up ~3.8x. so actual hit drop comes from more selector time causing smaller effective batching window.
olivia: possible fixes: 1) optimize tiebreaker to exit early; 2) cache tie results per-seqlen in fast path; 3) revert commit for rollout until optimized.
kai: +1 for a short revert to unblock the release pipeline. we should also prepare a micro-optimization PR to follow.
raj: will open revert PR now (revert c4f7a9d). tagging @olivia for perf followup.
olivia: opening followup: i'll try the cache-by-seqlen approach and measure. rough plan: small LRU keyed by (model_id, seq_len, kernel_family) with TTL ~10s for bench runs.
morgan: for the immediate rollout blocker, revert PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/2290 (revert kernel-autoselect tiebreaker). CI running.
perf-bot: [ci] PR 2290: integration checks started. microbench will run post-merge.
li: re-run microbench against revert branch locally — hit-rate back to baseline within noise (~0.5%).
raj: CI for revert looks green on perf stage. will merge if no objections.
morgan: merge after a short soak on canary; but this was blocking the release so prioritize. also create a follow-up tracking issue with perf numbers and proposed optimizations.
olivia: creating issue: #INV-711 "kernel-autoselect tiebreaker perf followup" with flamegraphs and bench diffs.
kai: thanks all. good triage. after revert and canary, we should add a microbench unit test that exercises selector CPU and prevents future regressions (threshold at +2% selector CPU).
morgan: agreed — adding that to the followup. closing the loop once PR 2290 merges and canary passes. :thumbsup:
